lead.text: Tretåig hackspett är en svartvit hackspett som helt saknar rött i fjäderdräkten.
Den är starkt bunden till gran och häckar i Sverige i barr- och blandskog med mycket döda och döende träd.

fieldMarks.text: Svartvit fjäderdräkt helt utan rött eller rosa
Vit rygg med svarta ränder, mörka sidor och vitt ögonbrynsstreck
Hanen har gul till orangegul hjässa, honan svartgrå och ungfåglar gul

voice.text: Det vanligaste lätet liknar större hackspettens men är mer dämpat, ungefär gyg eller gygg, ibland ett hårdare kyk.
Den hörs mer sällan än större hackspett och lätena är mjukare.
Trumvirvlarna är mycket långa, ofta 1,1 till 1,4 sekunder för 20 slag, och har accelererande takt.

lead.text: The Eurasian Three-toed Woodpecker is a black-and-white woodpecker with no red at all in its plumage.
It is strongly tied to spruce and in Sweden breeds in coniferous and mixed forest with plenty of dead and dying trees.

fieldMarks.text: Black-and-white plumage with no red or pink at all
White back with black bars, dark flanks and a white stripe above the eye
Male has a yellow to orange-yellow crown, female blackish grey, juveniles yellow

voice.text: The commonest call resembles a Great Spotted Woodpecker's but is more muted, roughly gyg or gygg, sometimes a harder kyk.
It is heard less often than Great Spotted Woodpecker and its calls are softer.
The drum rolls are very long, often 1.1 to 1.4 seconds for 20 strikes, and have an accelerating rhythm.

whereWhen.text: In Sweden it breeds regularly south to a line from northern Dalsland through Närke and Västmanland to central Uppland.
About 45 percent of the Swedish population is estimated to live in Lappland.
It is reported most in September and October, and its share of all bird reports is highest in Jämtland.
It is red-listed in Sweden as Near Threatened.

behaviour.text: Its main food is larvae, pupae and immature adult insects of bark beetles, weevils, jewel beetles and longhorn beetles, among others.
It rings spruces by pecking small holes in the trunk and sucking out the sap.
The pair usually excavates a new nest hole each year in a dead or dying conifer.
It is not particularly shy and often lets people come within five metres before flying off.

text.text: The Eurasian Three-toed Woodpecker is slightly smaller than Great Spotted Woodpecker and is easily told apart by having no red at all in its plumage.
